content: Truth is one; the wise call it by many names.
author: Sanskrit Subhashitas
sourceWork: Ekam sat vipra bahudha vadanti (एकं सद्विप्रा बहुधा वदन्ति) — Rigveda I.164.46
explanation: Human languages, cultural dialects, and religious traditions are different paths up the same mountain. Sectarian bigots argue endlessly over whose trail map has the prettier calligraphy, while the wise pilgrim simply walks up the rock until reaching the summit.
practicalInsight: Look past cultural differences or divergent religious phrasing today. Seek the universal golden thread of truth beneath.
reflectionPrompt: Where has dogmatic sectarianism prevented you from recognizing divine truth when spoken in an unfamiliar dialect?
